permissions.pageSubtitle: Who can do what, and where it applies — six places, in the order you would ask.
permissions.questionPeople: Find a person, see everything they can do, and change it.
permissions.questionTemplates: What each kind of person gets automatically.
permissions.questionRules: Who is allowed to have what — and why something cannot be granted.
permissions.questionWhere: Which programs, ventures and courses each relationship covers.
permissions.questionHistory: What changed, who changed it, and why.
permissions.questionOperations: Run the jobs that change access for many people at once, and see who they would affect.
permissions.operationsIntro: Two jobs act on everyone at once. Both are additive and idempotent: they never overwrite an individual grant, and an explicit block on a person always wins over anything applied here.
permissions.operationsReconcileBody: Reads every contextual relationship — venture founder, program facilitator, program manager — and applies the capabilities that relationship justifies. Access granted by a relationship that has ended is withdrawn. Program access carries the program's end date, so it stops by itself when the program ends.
permissions.operationsReconcileConfirm: This will re-derive capability grants for every person holding a contextual relationship. Existing individual grants are never overwritten, and explicit blocks are never removed. Run it now?
permissions.operationsReadinessBody: Read-only. For each person holding a program assignment it shows what has been applied, what the next re-derive would change, and which capabilities they hold today that their assignment does not justify — the list that would disappear if access became strictly assignment-derived.
permissions.operationsTruncated: Only the first 200 people are shown. Re-run the report to see the rest after reconciling.
permissions.operationsFailed: The operation could not be completed.
permissions.programScopeBody: The measurement that makes the where-it-applies rule for programmes safe to switch on, plus the repair for the one thing that would block it. Read-only until you record a manager.
permissions.programScopeFailed: The programme access report could not be loaded.
permissions.programScopeUnmanagedBody: The where-it-applies rule matches a person to a programme through the manager relationship. A running programme with nobody recorded as its manager can therefore match nobody at all, so switching the rule on before repairing this would make the programme unreachable to everyone except the portfolio identity.
permissions.programScopeUnmanagedEmpty: Every running programme has a manager recorded.
permissions.programScopeAssignBody: Recording a manager is a change to the programme, not to this console: the new manager receives the access the assignment justifies, and the previous manager is reconciled at the same time. An individual grant and an explicit block are never touched.
permissions.programScopeAssignForbiddenTitle: This needs the programme edit capability
permissions.programScopeAssignForbidden: Changing who runs a programme is a programme write, so it needs the "{capability}" capability. Ask an administrator who holds it, or grant it to yourself in Templates. Nothing was changed.
permissions.programScopeAssignFailedTitle: The manager could not be recorded
permissions.programScopeAssignFailed: The manager could not be recorded.
permissions.programScopeAssignUnchanged: Already the recorded manager — nothing changed.
permissions.programScopeAssignNoChanges: No access was applied or withdrawn.
permissions.programScopeHoldersBody: Everyone whose template grants programme management. The number that decides whether the rule can be switched on is how many of them would be left attached to no running programme.
permissions.programScopeHoldersEmpty: Nobody holds a template that grants programme management.
permissions.programScopeSplitBody: The seeded programme-manager template grants programme management together with two unrelated powers, which is why the rule cannot simply be narrowed inside that template — narrowing it there would also remove those powers. A trimmed portfolio template has already been created for this; it stays inert until the default is repointed.
permissions.programScopeRemovalsTitle: What the portfolio template would stop granting
permissions.programScopeRemovalsEmpty: The portfolio template grants nothing outside programme management.
permissions.programScopeRepointBody: Open the trimmed template in Templates and use the default-for control to point the programme-manager identity at it. Until the default is repointed, that template grants nobody anything.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultTitle: The click at the end of the split
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultBody: Creating the trimmed portfolio template changed nobody. Pointing the programme-manager role default at it is what stops granting the unrelated powers to everyone who resolves through that identity. Read the impact first: nothing is written until you confirm.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultLoadFailed: The impact of the repoint could not be read.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultReadForbiddenTitl: Reading the impact needs a matrix permission
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultReadForbidden: Reading the impact is a permissions-matrix read, so it needs the "{capability}" capability. Ask an administrator who holds it. Nothing was changed.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultImpactBody: Read-only, and read before the write: this is what the trimmed template would stop granting, and how many people it reaches. Loading it changed nothing.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultConfirmBody: Everyone who resolves through the programme-manager identity stops being granted the capabilities below — {n} person(s) today. It can be pointed back at any time, and the change is recorded in the audit trail.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultForbiddenTitle: This needs the capability assignment permission
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultForbidden: Repointing a role default is a permission-configuration change, so it needs the "{capability}" capability. Ask an administrator who holds it, or grant it to yourself in Templates. Nothing was changed.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultFailedTitle: The default could not be repointed
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultFailed: The role default could not be repointed.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultResultPointed: The programme-manager role default now points at {profile}.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultResultRemovedNone: The previous default was granting nothing of its own.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultAlready: The programme-manager role default already points at the portfolio template — nothing was changed.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultUnchanged: The default was not repointed and no capability was removed.
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultCustomizedTitle: Left alone — this default was set by hand
permissions.programPortfolioDefaultCustomized: This role default was customised by hand, so it is not overwritten: a deliberate choice is somebody's decision to revisit, not an error to repair. Nothing was changed.
permissions.programScopeCoverageTitle: Where the rule does not reach
permissions.programScopeCoverageBody: The rule is always on: it applies to every write surface below without a switch. It matches a person to a program through the assignment they hold, so what an administrator still needs to see is the opposite question — which surfaces it does NOT yet cover. Anything listed as partial keeps working for everyone until its own counterpart is converted, so it must not be read as closed.
permissions.programScopeCoverageSummary: Surfaces still outside the rule are listed above. Converting them is a code change, not a configuration one.
permissions.programScopeWaveCovers_content: Editing and archiving a programme's own content
permissions.programScopeWaveCovers_enrollment: Programme invitations, adding and removing participants
permissions.programScopeWaveCovers_groups: Cohorts and groups, and KPI weights
permissions.overviewLoadFailed: Could not load the overview data.
permissions.overviewContextAllMapped: Every contextual role maps to a profile
permissions.overviewScopeHint: Predicates implemented — verification only, not enforced
permissions.modelStripHint: Eligibility decides who may ever receive a feature; the profile and grants decide what the person holds; scope decides which records it applies to — always read from live data.
permissions.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, email, or CID...
permissions.advancedHint: Grant or block these rights for THIS person only, on top of what they inherit. They are enforced exactly like the four rights above — unlike the report, this section changes something.
permissions.advancedEmpty: No privileged capability is available for this selection.
permissions.capOriginProfileFallback: Inherited from the profile in force
permissions.capOriginSuperAdmin: Granted by the Super Admin bypass
permissions.personRightsHint: Pick a level chip to grant it to this person, use Block to deny a right they would otherwise inherit, and Restore to undo a block.
permissions.personIneligibleSectionsNote: A section marked Not eligible is shown read-only: this person cannot be granted a new right there (change the rules first), but their existing grant or block stays visible and can still be undone.
permissions.personNoSections: No section from the catalogue is available to edit here.
permissions.personAccessLoadFailed: Could not load this person's access.
permissions.personAccessUnavailable: No access data was returned for this person.
permissions.catalogLoadFailed: Could not load the section catalogue — no right can be listed without it.
permissions.noDefaultsHint: Use the Set Role Default Profile button to assign a default profile
permissions.defaultAccessHint: Role Defaults = the capabilities automatically given to everyone with this role (via their default Access Profile).
permissions.catalogUnavailable: Could not load the capability catalog — the feature list may be incomplete. Reload to retry.
permissions.profileInUseWarning: This profile is currently assigned as the default access profile for {roles}. Changes will affect users who inherit this profile.
permissions.eligibilityMatrixHint: E = eligible · D = explicitly denied · — = unset (fail-closed). Click a cell to edit that identity.
permissions.eligibilityImpactHint: This change removes eligibility, but access templates still grant the affected capabilities to this identity. Nothing has been saved yet — confirm to apply the change anyway (the templates themselves are not modified).
permissions.eligibilityNoPermission: You do not have permission to modify eligibility (permissions.configure_eligibility is required)
permissions.eligibilityReadOnly: Read-only — you do not hold the permissions.configure_eligibility capability
permissions.eligibilityHint: Eligibility defines who MAY receive a feature. It does not grant access — capabilities (Default Access profiles / Individual Access grants) decide what the person can actually do.
permissions.ineligibleCapsRole: Role {role} is not eligible for these features:
permissions.ineligibleCapsHint: The check covers every role this template serves. Add the role to those features in Rules → Feature eligibility, then save again.
permissions.eligibilityLegend: Eligible = may receive the feature. Not eligible = explicitly denied (deny wins). Unset = no row (missing rows fail closed to deny). Changes apply immediately to the authorization resolver.
permissions.profilesIntro: Access Profiles define what capabilities a user gets. Each role has a default profile; users can be assigned a specific profile to override the role default.
permissions.profilePickerHint: Choose a profile to view and edit its permissions.
permissions.assignHint: This overrides the user's role default profile. Set profile to empty to remove the override.
permissions.selectProfileRemoveOverride: -- Select profile (leave empty to remove override) --
permissions.selectProfilePrompt: Choose a profile from the list to view and edit its permissions.
permissions.profileChangeAffectsUsers: Changes will affect every user who inherits this profile.
permissions.defaultForNone: Not a default for anyone yet.
permissions.rolesAssignedHint: Roles that receive this profile by default.
permissions.profileEligibilityFilterHint: Showing only features that the role(s) using this profile are eligible for: {roles}
permissions.profileNoRolesHint: This profile is not the default profile of any role, so no feature is shown. Assign it to a role to configure it.
permissions.profileNoRolesEmpty: Assign this profile to a role — the features shown depend on what its roles are eligible for.
permissions.profileNoEligibleFeatures: None of this profile's roles are eligible for any feature — nothing to show.
permissions.hiddenStoredTitle: Capabilities still stored but not shown above
permissions.hiddenStoredHint: These capabilities are still saved in this template and still granted to everyone who inherits it, but they are no longer offered here: their feature is not eligible for the template's roles, the module has no dashboard section, or the capability itself no longer exists in the product. Remove them — or restore what is missing — before saving.
permissions.viewBaseHint: View is the base capability: checking any other capability also checks View, and unchecking View clears the module's other capabilities.
permissions.subsectionLevelHint: One access level per feature — its subsections are protected by the same modules, so choosing a level here applies to the whole feature.
permissions.viewRequiredMsg: View is required — disable the other capabilities before removing it.
permissions.responsibilitiesIntro: Responsibilities define operational ownership — what dashboards, navigation, and reports a user sees. They are NOT permissions.
permissions.responsibilitiesSearchPlaceholder: Search user by name, email, or CID...
permissions.responsibilityAccessIntro: Choose which roles can actually use the feature each responsibility grants. The warnings across the app read this configuration and it applies immediately. This is the LAST place where a role — rather than a capability or a profile — decides access; every other surface is capability-based.
permissions.auditSearch: Search actor, target, action, module, capability or details…
permissions.auditFilterPersonActive: Filtered to the changes recorded about ONE person. Clear the filter to see the whole portfolio.
permissions.governanceIntro: Operational overview of membership and permission activity. Informational only — no automatic changes are made from here.
permissions.whyMembershipNotContributing: Expired membership does not contribute to access
permissions.whyAccountIntact: Membership expiration never deletes the account — it only stops group-derived access.
permissions.contextRolesHint: Maps each contextual role (what someone is inside a Program / Venture / Learning / Investor context) to the access profile that seeds their capabilities. Applied since Phase 6: an active venture founder receives the mapped profile's capabilities as additive grants, withdrawn when the relationship ends. A role without a mapping applies nothing — shown as a gap, never hidden.
permissions.contextRolesStatusPill: Applied at the membership boundary — venture founders (Phase 6)
permissions.contextRolesLoadFailed: Could not load the context-role registry.
permissions.contextRolesReasonPlaceholder: Reason for these changes (optional — recorded in the audit log)
permissions.contextRolesHolderHint: Holder counts are informational — how many relationships of this kind exist today.
permissions.liveCheckHint: Read-only. Verifies what the Scope Engine decides for a real person and a real record — running a check grants and changes nothing.
permissions.liveCheckUserPlaceholder: cid or pick from the list
permissions.liveCheckNoResource: No record id supplied — nothing decided
permissions.liveCheckListFailed: People list unavailable — type a CID instead.
permissions.peopleHint: What can this person do — and why? Pick a person to see every capability decomposed into its sources (Profile | Group | Grant | Restriction), the effective result with its reason, and what the Scope Engine currently resolves — then change their access in the panel below.
permissions.peopleSelectPrompt: Select a person to see their access.
permissions.peopleListFailed: Could not load the people list.
permissions.personPickerHint: Choose a person to see their access below and change it.
permissions.peopleMatrixReportHint: Read-only report: what this person can do right now, and where each right comes from. The panel below is where the access is changed.
permissions.peopleReportLoadFailed: Could not load this person's capability report.
permissions.peopleMatrixRightNotHeld: Offered by this section, not held
permissions.peopleMatrixRightNotOffered: Not a right of this section
permissions.peopleContextsTitle: Contexts — what this person is part of
permissions.peopleContextsNone: No program, venture or course relationship.
permissions.peopleContextsPartial: Could not read: {kinds} — this list may be incomplete.
permissions.peopleContextsNote: Contexts are additive: they never replace the identity above. Each one shows the scope it resolves to, and the capability list below shows what it adds up to. An empty capability list therefore means "no grants", not "no access".
permissions.identityGroupsNote: The matrix lists baseline identities (Super Admin, Staff, Member). Context roles (Participant, Facilitator, Investor, Founder) are ceilings too, but they are held per relationship — open one in the identity editor to configure it; it never becomes the person's platform identity.
permissions.peopleScopeEmpty: No scope policy resolved for this person.
permissions.peopleScopeNote: Read-only verification. Scope is enforced server-side — the venture surfaces use venture_own today; the remaining surfaces follow as they migrate.
permissions.whyScopeNote: Scope is decided per record at the data layer — this drawer explains the capability, not the record.
permissions.peopleTableAria: Access matrix (scrolls horizontally on small screens)
permissions.scopePoliciesIntro: Record-level scope policies are enforced at the data layer by the Scope Engine (roadmap Phase 5). This registry is the governance surface for those policies — nothing here authorizes anything yet.
permissions.scopePoliciesStatus: Engine core implemented — verification only, not enforced (Phase 5)
permissions.scopePoliciesImplemented: Predicate implemented — verification only (not enforced on routes yet)
permissions.scopePoliciesRowVentureBody: Founder and team capabilities apply only to ventures the person belongs to.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowProgramBody: Program-staff and participant capabilities apply per program membership and assignment.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowProgramStaffedBody: The write side of the programme question. It matches people staffed on a programme — an assignment row of any kind, or being its named manager — and deliberately leaves out a learner's enrolment, because being enrolled in a programme must never be enough to change it.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowLearningBody: Learner capabilities apply to the learner's own enrollments.
permissions.scopePoliciesRowTeamBody: Team-entity access is limited to the team's own records.
permissions.reasonPlaceholder: Why is this change being made? (optional — recorded in the audit log)
permissions.reasonLabel: Reason recorded in the permission audit log
permissions.matrixNoDefaultProfileHint: This identity has no default access profile yet — set one in Access Profiles / Role Defaults before editing capabilities here.
permissions.matrixNoPendingChanges: No pending changes for this module.
permissions.userMatrixHint: Why can this user do what they do? Pick a user to see every capability decomposed into its sources — Profile | Group | Grant | Restriction — with the Effective result. Scope is a separate column (engine arrives in a later phase).
permissions.userMatrixEmpty: No capability grants. Access that comes from a context is listed in the Contexts panel above.
permissions.userMatrixFootnote: Sources: profile (base), groups, individual grants; restrictions remove the capability entirely (they beat grants). Effective = any source minus restrictions. Scope displays as All until the scope engine (P4) ships — the server remains authoritative.
permissions.catalogHint: Read-only registry of every Feature → Module → Capability the enforcement layer understands. Locked modules (Super Admin-only decisions) and retired capabilities are marked, never hidden.
permissions.catalogNoModules: No modules mapped to this feature yet.
permissions.scopePoliciesHint: Planned for a later phase (P4): which data each capability may operate on (assigned ventures, own venture…).
permissions.groupsHint: Group capability editing lives in the governance screens; protected-organization rules are enforced by org_membership.
permissions.enforcementNoteHint: This center manages configuration and visibility. Authorization is enforced server-side on every API; hiding a menu is never authorization.
permissions.personRecentHint: The last few access changes recorded about this person. Read-only — the audit log cannot be edited, and the full history is one click away.
permissions.personRecentEmpty: No access change has been recorded about this person yet.
permissions.personRecentFailed: Could not load this person's recent changes.
permissions.scopeRecordsNone: No record resolves for this policy.
permissions.scopeVerifyPickHint: Read-only. Click a resolved record above to load it, then run the same check the engine uses.
permissions.scopeVerifyFailed: The scope check could not run.
permissions.riskConfirmBody: Nothing is blocked — confirm only if this is intended. This change touches {count} capability(ies) rated high or critical risk:
permissions.riskConfirmNote: Risk levels come from the capability catalog, not from this screen. The write is recorded in the audit log with your name and, when you typed one, your reason.
permissions.rollupToggleShow: What does a kind of person or a group get?
permissions.rollupTitle: What a kind of person or a group gets
permissions.rollupHint: Read-only. Choose a person type or a group to see the access it gets today, the template in force, and the features it may ever receive. Nothing here changes anything — the template editor is below.
permissions.rollupPickPrompt: Choose a person type or a group to see what it gets.
permissions.rollupTemplateNone: No default template — the legacy role defaults below are what applies to this person type.
permissions.rollupEmptyRole: No capability is configured for this person type.
permissions.rollupEmptyGroup: No capability is configured for this group.
permissions.rollupLegacyNote: These are the legacy role defaults (role_capabilities). They apply only while the role has no default template.
permissions.rollupGroupNote: Group capabilities are ADDITIVE: they add to whatever the person already holds from their profile and never replace it.
permissions.rollupCeilingNote: A feature with no row at all is closed: the identity may never receive it. Denied means an explicit row says no.
permissions.rollupLoadFailed: Could not load the rollup data.
